subject: Re: ACME POC - evaluation methodology & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC - initial success criteria / quick follow-up

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the walk-through. Priya and I sketched some high-level success criteria for the POC and wanted to share to make sure we're aligned before the formal eval plan: 

- Latency: 95th < 400ms for single-turn generation on our typical 512-token prompts
- Quality: human-graded relevance >= 85% on priority prompt set (see attached sample)
- Cost: projected per-1000-token cost <= $0.45 (incl. embeddings and reranking)
- Safety: zero PII leaks on our screened test cases

Next steps we discussed: you to share the formal evaluation template + recommended offline vs shadow approach; we to confirm internal owners and timelines. Can you send an initial eval plan by end of week?

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Search & AI
Acme Corporation

On Thu, Apr 29, 2027 at 11:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Great to meet you both — Jordan, Priya. Posting notes here and looping Dylan and Rachel for the eval methodology piece.
>
> - We can run a two-track POC: (A) offline evaluations on your labeled prompt set (fast, reproducible) and (B) online shadowing for a subset of live traffic (validates real-world behavior).
> - For offline: we'll use your priority prompt set + our grading rubric; results back in ~5 business days after you share data.
> - For shadow: 1-week shadow window with canary routing to our runtime; requires a sandboxed dataset and traffic mirror. Latency and end-to-end metrics during window.
>
> Attaching the POC evaluation template. I'll follow up with a proposed owner-level timeline by tomorrow.
>
> Cheers,
>Marissa
>Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
>Attachment: POC_Eval_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC - evaluation methodology & next steps

Jordan — here is the proposed evaluation plan and owners (per our call):

1) Offline eval (owner: Rachel Kim) — timeline: share labeled prompt set by Mon 5/3; Rachel to run grading and deliver a report by Fri 5/7. Metrics:
   - Relevance: top-1 human grade (0-100) aggregated; target >=85
   - Safety: automated PII check + manual review on flagged items
   - Semantic similarity (embedding-based) for reranking candidates

2) Shadow eval (owner: Dylan Brooks / infra) — timeline: prep mirror by 5/10, 1-week shadow from 5/12-5/19. Metrics:
   - Latency (p95)
   - Error rate / fallback frequency
   - Live quality sample: 200 manually reviewed cases across week

3) Cost projection (owner: Marissa Cole) — Marissa will run model/quantization scenarios and provide per-1k token cost estimate by 5/6.

Grading rubric summary (attached as grading_rubric.md):
- Score 0-3 per response across dimensions: Relevance, Correctness, Safety, Helpfulness
- Pass threshold: average >=2.5 across 100+ cases for primary prompts
- Failure modes logged with examples and severity tag (minor/major/blocker)

Open questions:
- Does Acme want the shadow to include reranking step or just raw generation? (re-ranking increases compute and may affect latency)
- Who is the internal sign-off for go/no-go after POC (product/engineering/infra)?

If that plan looks good I'll put these dates into a shared calendar invite and create the HubSpot tasks.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: grading_rubric.md

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC - evaluation methodology & next steps

Thanks — this is great and aligns with our internal thinking. A couple quick notes: 

- For the shadow: please include reranking; our UX team wants to validate end-to-end results. If cost/latency looks problematic we can do a targeted rerank subset for high-value queries.
- Go/no-go approver will be Meera Patel (Head of Search) — happy to loop her once we have offline results.
- We'll bundle and share the labeled prompt set (and a 5k-sample of live queries for shadow) by EOD Monday 5/3.

One ask: can you include a short example in the rubric showing how a "major" vs "minor" safety issue is scored? That will help our reviewers calibrate.

Thanks,
Priya
Product Manager, Search
Acme Corporation

Jordan/Priya — quick confirmation from infra side: we can mirror traffic into a shadow pool and include reranking, but reranking will require an extra quantization profile (adds ~15% CPU/GPU) — we'll include both data points in the week-of-5/12 run.

Action items I've put into HubSpot: Prep shadow mirror (Dylan, due 5/10), Run offline eval (Rachel, due 5/7), Cost scenario (Marissa, due 5/6). I'll send the calendar invites after you confirm the owners.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Dylan
